threads.body: Token extraction uses `getattr(... ) or (...)`, which will treat a legitimate token count of `0` as falsy and fall back to the dict lookup (or `None`), potentially dropping valid 0-valued usage. Prefer explicit `is None` checks (or a small helper) so `0` is preserved for both input and output tokens.

replies.body: Good catch — fixed in 91662ae. Verified upstream `claude-agent-sdk` `AssistantMessage.usage` / `ResultMessage.usage` are typed `dict[str, Any] | None`, so the `getattr(...) or (...)` pattern (which dropped legitimate `0` and also did nothing useful on a dict) was reduced to a direct `msg_usage.get("input_tokens")` / `msg_usage.get("output_tokens")`. The guard is now just `if msg_usage is not None and input_tokens is None`, so `0` is preserved for both input and output tokens.

Please update the PR description (or adjust the change) so reviewers can clearly understand whether behavior changed and which SDK fields are considered the authoritative sources.

replies.body: Good catch — the PR description was wrong. Updated the body to: (1) drop the "no code changes to scenario.py" claim, (2) explain that the old code targeted a nonexistent `AssistantMessage.message.*` shape and so was silently producing zero response attributes, (3) correct the Source column to reflect the actual SDK fields (`AssistantMessage.message_id`, `AssistantMessage.model`, `AssistantMessage.usage["..."]`), and (4) add `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` (also captured but previously omitted). Behavior change: response attributes that data.json claims are now actually emitted; before this PR they were not.
